title: The Mayflower Compact says the signers combine into a civil body politic
summary: The 1620 Mayflower Compact combines its signers into a civil body politic.
body: The Mayflower Compact says the signers covenant and combine themselves into a civil body politic to enact just and equal laws. The text is an agreement among the colonists. It does not mention, and does not grant rights to, the Wampanoag or other Native nations. The wording on the page includes: "in the Presence of God and one another, covenant and combine ourselves together into a civil Body Politick, for our better Ordering and Preservation, and Furtherance of the Ends aforesaid: And by Virtue hereof do enact, constitute, and frame, such just and equal Laws, Ordinances, Acts, Constitutions, and Officers, from time to time, as shall be thought most meet".
